system: Social Sciences: Communication and Interpersonal Skills
diagnosis: Impaired physician: duty to protect patients and intervene when a colleague cannot practice safely
mechanism: Physicians have a professional obligation to protect patients when a colleague's illness or substance use impairs safe practice. The immediate priority is to stop unsafe patient care and obtain appropriate institutional or supervisory assistance; subsequent evaluation, treatment, and reporting should follow applicable institutional policy, regulatory requirements, and law.
vignette: A resident is preparing an elective procedure with an attending physician. Just before the patient is brought into the procedure room, the resident notices that the attending smells strongly of alcohol, has slurred speech, and is unsteady while walking. The attending says, “I had a few drinks at lunch, but I can do this case. Do not make this a problem.” The procedure has not yet begun.
lead: Which of the following is the most appropriate action by the resident?
correct: Prevent the attending from participating in patient care and immediately seek appropriate supervisory or institutional assistance to ensure safe coverage and evaluation
distractors: Allow the attending to perform the procedure, then privately recommend a physician health program after the case
Ask the attending whether he personally feels capable of proceeding and defer to his judgment if he says yes
Wait for objective blood alcohol testing before taking action because impairment should not be presumed from behavior alone
Keep the observation confidential because no patient has yet been harmed and discuss it with the attending after the shift
distractor_notes: Referral for assistance is important, but it does not justify allowing a visibly impaired physician to continue patient care while patients are at immediate risk.
A physician who appears unable to practice safely should not be permitted to determine unilaterally that continued practice is safe; colleagues have a duty to intervene to protect patients.
The ethical duty to prevent unsafe care does not require delaying intervention until a laboratory test confirms impairment when observable behavior already raises a serious safety concern.
Confidentiality toward a colleague does not override the obligation to protect patients from unsafe practice. Appropriate assistance and escalation should occur promptly.
key_expl: The attending shows direct evidence of acute impairment immediately before patient care. The resident's first obligation is patient safety: intervene so the attending does not participate in the procedure and seek appropriate supervisory or institutional help for safe coverage and evaluation. AMA ethics guidance states that physicians should intervene when a colleague cannot practice safely, ensure that the colleague is no longer endangering patients, and seek assistance consistent with institutional policies, regulatory requirements, and applicable law. Immediate state-board reporting is not automatically the first or only step in every setting; the item therefore keys the broader, defensible duty to stop unsafe care and escalate appropriately.
objective: When a physician appears unable to practice safely because of impairment, protect patients by stopping unsafe clinical activity and promptly involving the appropriate supervisory or institutional process.
clues: attending asks trainee to ignore the impairment

sources.title: Physician Health & Wellness — AMA Code of Medical Ethics
sources.support: Physicians should not practice when their ability to do so safely is impaired by alcohol, controlled substances, another chemical agent, or a health condition; the profession has an obligation to promote safe and effective care.
